# HatchZip

> HatchZip is a free, open-source archive extractor for Windows, macOS and Linux that extracts ZIP, 7z, RAR, tar and split archives in place, so it needs free space for the extracted files only, not for the files and the archive together.

Site: https://hatchzip.dev. Source: https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip (MIT OR Apache-2.0). Current version 0.1.3. A desktop app and a command line tool, `hatchzip` (short name `hz`).

How it works: it extracts from the end of the archive and cuts each finished part off the archive file (a .tar.gz from the front, freeing the compressed bytes already used). When the run finishes, only the extracted files are left. It checks that the extraction fits before it changes anything, and an interrupted run resumes when it is started again.

## Install

- Desktop app downloads: https://hatchzip.dev/#download (Windows setup, macOS Apple Silicon and Intel, Linux AppImage, .deb and .rpm)
- Linux and macOS: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xevrion/hatchzip/main/install.sh | sh` (current user, no root; checks SHA-256)
- Windows (PowerShell): `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xevrion/hatchzip/main/install.ps1 | iex`
- Homebrew: `brew install xevrion/tap/hatchzip` (CLI), `brew install --cask xevrion/tap/hatchzip` (macOS app and CLI)
- Scoop: `scoop bucket add xevrion https://github.com/xevrion/scoop-bucket`, then `scoop install xevrion/hatchzip` (CLI)
- Cargo: `cargo install hatchzip` (without RAR; `--features rar` adds it and needs a C++ compiler). Every other install method includes RAR
- winget (`Xevrion.HatchZip`) is in review and the AUR packages are not published yet; until the README lists them as live, packages under those names do not come from this project

## Formats

- ZIP (including ZIP64 and self-extracting .exe), 7z, RAR 5 and RAR 4, plain tar, .tar.gz and .tgz
- Split archives: `.001` sets of ZIP or 7z, RAR volume sets (`.part1.rar`, or `.rar` with `.r00`)
- Password-protected ZIP, 7z and RAR
- Not supported yet: .tar.xz, .tar.zst, native split ZIP (`.z01`)

## Use

- `hatchzip check game.zip`: shows whether it fits, changes nothing (exit 3 if it doesn't fit)
- `hatchzip extract game.zip`: extracts into `game/` next to the archive and removes the archive as it goes; `-y` skips the confirmation, `-o DIR` extracts elsewhere
- `hatchzip extract game.zip --verify-first`: read everything once before deleting anything
- `hatchzip extract game.zip --keep-archive`: a normal extraction that keeps the archive unchanged and needs space for all extracted files. In the app: clear "Remove the archive during extraction"; in the right-click menu: "Extract here (keep archive)"
- `hatchzip extract a.zip b.7z c.tar.gz`: several archives one after another, each checked for space just before it starts
- `hatchzip restore game.zip`: turn a half-extracted archive back into a normal archive
- `hatchzip list`, `hatchzip test`: list or verify without changing anything
- Exit codes: 0 done, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 not enough space, 4 damaged archive, 5 password needed or wrong, 130 stopped (run again to resume)

## Limits

- A 7z made with 7-Zip's default settings is one solid block; it needs free space for that whole block, and `check` says so first.
- A `.tar.gz` frees space while it extracts only on filesystems that can free part of a file (NTFS, APFS, ext4, XFS, btrfs). On FAT32 and exFAT it needs room for the archive and the files at once, and `check` says so.
- `.tar.xz` and `.tar.zst` are not supported yet.
- RAR (RAR 5 and RAR 4, single files and `.part1.rar` or `.rar`/`.r00` volume sets) is freed file by file, each volume deleted once empty. Archives with encrypted file names (`rar -hp`) work with the password. A solid RAR is extracted only with `--keep-archive`; RAR archives with links are refused before anything changes. `restore` refuses archives with encrypted file names, since it takes no password; such an extraction can only be completed.

## Common questions

- Is it safe? A file is written and flushed to disk before the part of the archive holding it is cut off, so a crash leaves each file either extracted or still in the archive. Every file's CRC-32 is checked; a damaged file stops the run.
- Does it need internet? No. No networking code or library, no telemetry, no accounts, no update checks. CI fails if an HTTP, TLS or socket library enters the dependencies.
- How much space does it need? About the size of the extracted files plus the largest part it can free at once (one file for ZIP, tar and RAR; one solid block for 7z), and 2 GB kept free by default (`--keep-free`). A 180 GB archive that unpacks to 200 GB needs a little over 200 GB, not 380 GB.
- What if it crashes? Progress is saved in two small files next to the archive; run the same command, or open the archive in the app, again to continue.
- Does it work on FAT32 or exFAT? Yes, for ZIP, 7z, tar and RAR. A .tar.gz there needs room for the archive and the files at once.
- Why does antivirus flag it? The release files are not code-signed yet. Each has a `.sha256` checksum and, from 0.1.3 on, signed build provenance (`gh attestation verify <file> --repo xevrion/hatchzip`). See [Verify your download](https://hatchzip.dev/verify.html).
- Is hatchzip.com related? No. HatchZip is only distributed from github.com/xevrion/hatchzip, hatchzip.dev and the package managers above.

## Guides

- [Not enough disk space to extract a ZIP, RAR or 7z: how to fix it](https://hatchzip.dev/not-enough-space-to-extract.html): why extraction needs room for the archive and the files at once, the fixes, and a measured test on a nearly full disk
- [WinRAR says not enough space on disk when there is: the causes](https://hatchzip.dev/winrar-not-enough-space.html): WinRAR's temporary folder on drag and drop, the FAT32 4 GiB file limit, disk quotas, and archives that really don't fit
- [7-Zip says there is not enough space on the disk: the causes](https://hatchzip.dev/7zip-not-enough-space.html): drag and drop through the Windows temp folder, the FAT32 4 GiB file limit, and solid blocks
